plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and the payment rule (paying the second highest bid), the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, and bidders are rational, they won't bid their full value. A conservative estimate for the second highest bid is around half of the maximum value, or $10. To ensure winning against bids close to $10, I'll bid $10.10. My value is $27, so winning at this price yields a profit of $27 - $10.10 = $16.90.

Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * $20 = $13.33. To win with a high probability while minimizing overpayment, I will bid slightly above this, aiming for $14.00. My value is $16, so this ensures a positive expected profit.
